rounds.text: Megri Soft Ltd is heavily under-appreciated because its asset valuation fails to reflect its true underlying position, trading at a price-to-book ratio of 1.12x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.42x [E7]. The market capitalisation sits at a modest ₹ 25.6 Cr [E3], while the company aggressively builds for the future, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) surging by 39.3% to reach Rs 4.11 Cr in March 2026, indicating active growth spend underway [E38]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is expanding with the operating margin improving to 30% in TTM from 28% three years earlier [E27]. Conceded: compounded share price growth over 5 years is -14% [E21], and the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E4].

Megri Soft Ltd carries a premium valuation that is completely unsupported by its weak fundamental growth, trading at a steep P/E of 38.8x [E1] while its 5-year compounded sales growth crawls at a sluggish 6% [E14], significantly lagging the sector median sales growth of 11.6% [E65]. This expensive multiple is coupled with negative long-term shareholder wealth creation, demonstrated by compounded share price growth of -14% over 5 years, -6% over 3 years, and -15% over 1 year [E21, E22, E23]. Furthermore, the company offers zero return to investors in cash distribution, with a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Operational momentum is also showing cracks, evidenced by quarterly operating margins contracting by 2 percentage points down to 27% in June 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E28], alongside explicit flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E58]. Conceded: the company displays a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.12x [E2] and an operating margin of 30% in TTM [E27].

The bear’s focus on historical share price performance [E21, E22, E23] ignores the current inflection point where profit growth is now outpacing 1-year price growth by 35%, signaling a fundamental shift toward outperformance [E45]. While the bear highlights sluggish long-term sales growth [E14, E51], it overlooks the most recent data showing a 46% year-over-year surge in sales [E54] and strong sales growth momentum [E55]. The valuation is not "steep" when viewed through the lens of asset backing, as the P/B ratio of 1.12x is actually more attractive than the sector benchmark of 1.42x [E7]. Furthermore, the 39.3% increase in Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) [E38] demonstrates that the company is actively deploying capital for future growth, which explains the current focus on reinvestment over dividend payouts [E4]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], earnings growth is flagged as decelerating [E58], and quarterly operating margins contracted by 2 percentage points [E28]. Despite these short-term fluctuations, the company maintains a robust 30% TTM operating margin [E27] and profit growth exceeding 20% year-over-year [E57].

The bull’s reliance on a 46% year-over-year sales surge [E54] is undermined by the broader reality that compounded sales growth remains stuck at a meager 6% over the last five years [E14, E51], significantly trailing the sector median of 11.6% [E65]. While the bull cites an inflection point [E45], this is contradicted by the explicit flagging of decelerating earnings growth [E58] and a contraction in quarterly operating margins from 29% to 27% [E28]. Conceded: the company maintains a 30% TTM operating margin [E27] and profit growth exceeding 20% [E57]. However, this does not justify a P/E ratio of 38.8x [E1], which is more than double the sector benchmark of 18.13x [E6]. The bull’s optimism regarding CWIP [E38] ignores that this capital deployment has yet to translate into sustained shareholder value, as evidenced by the negative compounded share price growth over the past one, three, and five years [E21, E22, E23]. Ultimately, the lack of any dividend yield [E4] combined with a consistent history of share price decline suggests that the market remains unconvinced by the company's growth narrative.
